newsitem.title: CHILE: U.S. tycoon's proposed reserve in Chile under fire.
newsitem.headline: U.S. tycoon's proposed reserve in Chile under fire.

text.p: President Eduardo Frei has asked for a report on controversial plans by U.S. millionaire Douglas Tompkins to create a huge rainforest reserve in Chile's far south, a Frei aide said on Friday.
Tompkins' plan to turn woodlands he owns into a nature park has raised the hackles of nationalists and the powerful armed forces who accuse him of wanting to cut Chile in half.

"What we want to do is clarify once and forever all the doubts which have been raised," Frei chief of staff Juan Villarzu told reporters. "The only thing I am doing is putting together ... all the information which exists to give the president of the republic the most complete account, which can serve as basis for clearing up doubts over the issue."
The government has stepped up criticism of Tompkins, who owns more than 690,000 acres (280,000 hectares) of virgin forests stretching from Chile's Pacific coast to the Andean border with Argentina.
His land is one the last wilderness areas left in southern Chile and has spectacular scenery including dramatic snow-covered peaks, icy fjords and rare Andean larch forests.
Local media reported that Frei was surprised at the extent of Tompkins' land during a visit to the south in February.
Tompkins' opponents accuse him of building unauthorised landing strips on his property and of depopulating the sensitive border area by pressuring settlers to sell their farms at deflated prices.
Villarzu said he had a meeting recently with U.S. Ambassador Gabriel Guerra Mondragon who expressed concern over the controversy surrounding Tompkins and the government's stance towards the project.
"I told him that what the government is interested in is checking that Chilean laws are obeyed and inasfar as this is done Mr Tompkins is welcome," Villarzu said.
Supporters of the project accuse Tompkins' detractors of acting in the interests of big logging companies that want to move into the area.
